articles.title: Celtic 3-2 Besiktas: Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand come off bench to inspire Hoops to first Europa League win
articles.summary: Report as Celtic secure their first Europa League win; Junior Olaitan put the visitors ahead from the spot after a needless challenge from Jordan Lotomba; substitute Callum Osmand equalised with his first touch; Camilo Duran scored either side of Orkun Kokcu's strike to secure the points
articles.body:
Junior Olaitan's goal - a rebound after Sam Johnstone saved his penalty - looked like condemning Celtic to a fifth consecutive European defeat for the first time in the club's history.

But the introduction of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan just after the hour was a masterstroke from O'Neill.

Osmand fired in the equaliser with his first touch before setting up Duran to round the goalkeeper and put the Hoops ahead.

With five minutes left, Celtic suffered a major blow as Orkun Kokcu came on for Besiktas to fire into the bottom corner from 25 yards.

But Duran was not done. He picked up the ball from Kieran Tierney and poked it into the net two minutes later to restore the Hoops' lead.

Celtic remain in the bottom 12 of the Europa League table, but, with four games left, they still have a chance of reaching the knockout stages.

Remember, remember the fifth of November? It is a night the Celtic fans are unlikely to forget.

8: CHANCE! Some brilliant play from Celtic, all starting from Sebastian Tounekti. He eventually crosses the ball into the box for Benjamin Nygren, who sends it wide.

11: BLOCK! Cameron Carter-Vickers recovers to stop Leandro Trossard from getting a shot away for the visitors.

26: CHANCE! Kasper Hogh is waiting in the box for Tounekti's cross, but it is diverted out for a corner.

50: SAVE! James Forrest with the first shot on target! He picks the ball up out wide and drives into the box. He fires low towards Alexander Nubel, who gets down to save.

52: PENALTY TO BESIKTAS! Jordan Lotomba lunges in for a needless challenge on Ernest Poku, and the referee points to the spot.

54: GOAL BESIKTAS! Johnstone pushes Olaitan's spot-kick back out, but he taps in the rebound.

59: CHANCE! Lotomba runs all the way from his own half to the Besiktas box but cannot get a shot away.

65: GOAL CELTIC! Osmand makes an immediate impact, firing into the net with his first touch.

67: SAVE! Liam Scales' deflected header is pushed over the bar by Nubel.

79: GOAL CELTIC! Duran collects the pass from Osmand, rounds the 'keeper and fires Celtic in front.

85: GOAL BESIKTAS! Kokcu takes aim from around 25 yards and his strike finds the bottom corner.

87: GOAL CELTIC! Duran picks up the ball from Tierney, takes his time and pokes the ball into the net. The hosts are back in front.

Sky Sports' Gordon Duncan at Celtic Park:

"You have to wonder where that second-half performance has been for the last two months.

"Quality, desire, running power - all of the things the team's been accused of lacking recently were there.

"It's hard to overstate just how difference-making the substitutes were.

"Two goals for Camilo Duran and a goal and an assist for Callum Osmand. Inspired changes or the wrong team to begin with?

"A discussion for another day, perhaps. It's all about a Europa League campaign possibly back on track and a big lift in the general mood around the club."

"We've given ourselves a chance because of the result.

"The game was pretty difficult but we came through it, we came through it with flying colours. I just said to the team, they were a credit to the football club and you can't get a bigger accolade than that.

"We were doing fine after the penalty goes in, but we came roaring back and the substitutes made a big, big difference as well too, got a lot of pace up front, but I was just delighted with the whole team.

"It might just give us a platform to charge on. It's not going to be easy, but this definitely gives us a chance.

"A terrific win, in every aspect. I thought we played some really lovely stuff as well too, and they are a very fine side.

"Some of these lads who have been at the football club for some time, who have been big winners, I thought they came to the fore, and also some of the lads who joined us, big performances.

"It's hard to single people out, Tierney was fantastic for us, back four did really well, Colby coming on to a game as well too, he's got a massive heart, and wee Mika Baur was magnificent for us in the middle of the pitch.

"You have to find the net, and we did that, Callum comes on, first touch, puts the ball in the net, that's really difficult.

"Duran who's been fabulous for us the whole season, regardless of where he plays."

articles.title: Kolo Muani guía a la Juve por el atajo de la Europa League
articles.standfirst: Sufrida victoria frente al AZ a domicilio con gol y asistencia del ex del PSG
articles.summary: Sufrida victoria frente al AZ a domicilio con gol y asistencia del ex del PSG
articles.body: La Juventus, a pesar del último triunfo frente al Nápoles, ya está completamente descolgado de la lucha por el 'Scudetto'... y marcha a seis puntos de distancia del Top-4. La Europa League, sin embargo, aparece como un 'atajo' para meterse en Champions en caso de levantar el título. De momento, se mantienen invictos e, impulsados por Kolo Muani, hicieron los deberes contra a domicilio contra un AZ (1-2) que les hizo sufrir en el tramo final. Spalletti recuperó la línea de tres centrales y, un días, volvió a apostar por la doble punta formada por Kolo Muani y Woltemade... con Alajbegovic unos metros por detrás. El 'morbo', eso sí, lo ponía el duelo entre los hermanos Koopmeiners, Peer y Teun, en los respectivos centros del campo de AZ y Juventus. Entró 'enchufado' al partido un Kolo Muani que necesita reivindicarse. Nada más ponerse el balón en juego, mandó un aviso con un disparo cruzado desde dentro del área que no se fue demasiado desviado. En el 19', sin embargo, firmó una acción colosal por banda derecha, con sombrero incluido, para terminar asistiendo a un Teun Koopmeiners que ajustó su remate a la cepa del poste desde la corona del área llegando desde atrás. Tenía el día Kolo Muani y, en el 37', fue el encargado de duplicar la renta para la Juventus. Él mismo recuperó el balón en el sector derecho, tiró una pared con Woltemade y conectó un 'zurdazo' ajustado al palo largo. Suma cuatro goles el galo esta temporada... y tres de ellos han llegado en Europa League. Pasada la hora de encuentro, saltó al césped un Kees Smit que trató de entonar al AZ. La Juventus, mientras, trató de hacerse fuerte con la entrada de Bremer. Hasta entonces, Vicario apenas había tenido que intervenir. Meerdink, sin embargo, recortó distancias en el 88' a pase de Dijkstra y, con el tiempo prácticamente cumplido, el VAR le salvó la vida a los de Spalletti. La temporada apuntaba a drama en el Olympique de Marsella. Poco a poco, sin embargo, han empezado a crecer y, por fin, han conseguido trasladarlo a la Europa League. Y es que, después de caer en las tres primeras jornadas, lograron un triunfo de prestigio en el BayArena ante el Bayer Leverkusen de Carles Martínez Novell (0-1) saldado con un gran gol de Amine Gouiri en la segunda parte. Sufrió mucho más de lo esperado el Benfica (3-1). Sobre todo, después de adelantarse nada más adelantar el choque por medio de Rafa Silva. Pero, cuando más estaba apretando el Lech Poznan, Prestianni se inventó una jugada de genio para duplicar la ventaja y dejar en anécdota el tanto de Bengtsson. Ya en el descuento, sentenció Sudakov con un remate sutil desde el interior del área. El Dinamo Zagreb apenas sumaba una victoria en esta Europa League y venía de sufrir una dura derrota en casa frente al NEC Nimega. Pero, gracias a dos goles de Stojkovic y Beljo en la primera parte, le endosaron su primera derrota a un Sunderland (0-2) centrado en evitar el descenso a Championship. Dos victorias en cuatro jornadas para un Torreense que tiró de épica para tumbar al Ararat-Armenia (3-2). Escasos minutos después de firmar el 1-0, Jorge Aguirre fue expulsado y abrió la puerta para que los visitantes le diesen la vuelta al marcador. Sin embargo, la roja de Joao Bravim en el 76' volvió a meter en el partido a los lusos, que remontaron gracias a dos goles de Javi Vázquez y Drammeh en el descuento.

articles.title: La AFE solicita al Juez Único de Competiciones que aplace todos los partidos de Segunda
articles.standfirst: El sindicato dice que la petición responde al sentir mayoritario de los futbolistas de la categoría, que quieren mostrar su apoyo y solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: El sindicato dice que la petición responde al sentir mayoritario de los futbolistas de la categoría, que quieren mostrar su apoyo y solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel
articles.body: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE) lanzó un comunicado en el que anuncia que va a solicitar al Juez Único de Competiciones Profesionales que aplace la próxima jornada de LaLiga Hypermotion, la decimotercera, al completo tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel. AFE señala que la petición responde al sentir mayoritario de los futbolistas de la categoría, que quieren mostrar su apoyo y solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel. Es es el comunicado de AFE: La Asociación de Futbolistas Españoles (AFE), tras mantener conversaciones con todos los capitanes de los equipos de Segunda División, ha remitido una carta al Juez Único de Competiciones Profesionales de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) en la que solicita el aplazamiento de los partidos correspondientes a la próxima jornada de la segunda categoría del fútbol masculino español. Esta petición responde al sentir mayoritario de los futbolistas de la categoría, que consideran que, por respeto, solidaridad y compañerismo hacia Jesús de Miguel, no debería disputarse la jornada en las actuales circunstancias. La gran mayoría de los capitanes y de los jugadores consultados por AFE han trasladado su preocupación y malestar por esta situación, mostrando su apoyo y solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel, compañero de categoría. Los futbolistas entienden que este momento requiere de empatía y humanidad. AFE espera que el Juez Único de Competiciones Profesionales tenga en consideración la petición trasladada y las circunstancias que la motivan. AFE considera que en este tipo de situaciones, el fútbol debe actuar con sensibilidad con las personas que forman parte de él. El comunicado de la AFE llega tras el anuncio por parte de LaLiga y de la RFEF de que la jornada se disputará al completo en LaLiga EA Sports y se aplazarán tres de los once partidos en LaLiga Hypermotion: Castellón–Eibar, Granada–Tenerife y Andorra–Mallorca, además del Costa Adeje Tenerife-Deportivo Alavés de la Liga F Moeve. Tanto la patronal de los clubes como la Federación han preparado un homenaje a Jesús de Miguel. Los futbolistas de todos los equipos saldrán al terreno de juego con una camiseta especial y los partidos se detendrán en la primera pausa que haya después del minuto 9 de partido.

articles.title: Oliver Glasner says Nottingham Forest cannot rely on 'flower power' for success
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner insists his Nottingham Forest side cannot survive on "flower power" as he tries to strike a balance between trust and respect at the club.
articles.body:
Oliver Glasner insists his struggling Nottingham Forest side cannot survive on "flower power" as he tries to find a combination of trust and respect from his squad.

Forest are 19th in the Premier League and winless and goalless at home in the top flight.

Last weekend's 2-0 defeat at Brentford was a fourth defeat in five games as Glasner warned there would be no more compromises after his summer arrival, and he has underlined his standards.

"These are my two values I will never negotiate about, this is trust and respect," he said.

"It can't be one, so if it's just respect, I would say that's military. Then, after a few months of the national service, you are pleased when you can leave.

"When it's just trust, it's a flower power, just flying. Everybody can do what he wants and it's nice and great - Woodstock - but it's not high-performance Woodstock.

"Military is [high performance], to be honest, because otherwise this huge organisation couldn't work, and I felt we had too much Woodstock.

"We need a good balance between Woodstock, having fun, but also military, high performance. That's the most important thing, high performance, because that's what we get paid for, that's our job. If we have this - fly."

When asked by BBC Sport if he should have told his players sooner Glasner said: "I always ask myself this question - should I have done it earlier?

"Of course, maybe two or three times I felt it's time and then I thought 'no, come on Oliver, be patient and maybe things change'.

"Then it seemed to be the same game [ Brentford ] like the last ones, so I felt I have to say it now because otherwise things won't change."

Glasner is not under immediate pressure and remains in close communication with the Forest hierarchy, with stability desired after four managers last season.

The 52-year-old has made a positive impression with his work and methods, even if there have been some obvious grumbles from players who are not playing, and there remains a desire to stay calm.

"I'm always in contact with the ownership," Glasner said. "It's not always Mr [Evangelos] Marinakis because he has other stuff to do, but there is his son [Miltiadis], George [Syrianos, chief football officer] and Pedro [Ferreira, technical director] here at the training ground, and Theodore [Giannikos] the CEO.

"There's always communication - and that's a good thing, because everybody understands better why I am how I am. I never say what's best for Oliver Glasner, because I don't feel important. I will always say what I believe is best for Nottingham Forest , for the club.

"I don't like to accept things if I feel they are wrong. My addiction is to succeed with Nottingham Forest and, right now, I have failed. Then I get really upset with myself because I want to meet the expectations of the players, owner and the fans.

"Right now, I've failed and that's why I blame myself most."

articles.title: Rashford: "Si Lamine gana siete Balones de oro no me sorprenderá"
articles.standfirst: El excompañero del azulgrana se deshace en elogios hacia él y lo compara con Messi
articles.summary: El excompañero del azulgrana se deshace en elogios hacia él y lo compara con Messi
articles.body: A Marcus Rashford solo le ha hecho falta un año para darse cuenta del talento que desprende Lamine Yamal en estos primeros años de carrera profesional. En un encuentro con seguidores del Manchester United en el Ambassadors' Lounge d'Old Trafford, el delantero inglés no se cortó a la hora de elogiar a Lamine e, incluso, de compararlo con Leo Messi. "Creo mucho en el talento de este chico, si llega a ganar siete Balones de Oro no me sorprenderá. Ha terminado segundo, tercero y octavo. ¿Y a la edad de qué, 19 años?". "Antes de irme del Barça, le dije a Lamine Yamal que había jugado con algunos jugadores muy talentosos, pero que él está por encima de todos ellos. Nunca he visto a un jugador de esa edad con tanto talento como él, es lo más cerca que alguien puede estar del nivel de Messi a lo largo de los años". "Es un jugador increíble. Probablemente nunca veremos a otro jugador en nuestra vida en términos de un genio completo como Leo". "Marcó una cantidad estúpida de goles este año y una cantidad estúpida de asistencias. Le envié un mensaje de texto el otro día y le dije que se lo merecía”. "No podía seguir jugando contra el United cada temporada. Si el United no es una opción, le dije a mi agente que me llevase al extranjero, no me lleves a otro club de la Premier League".

articles.title: El fichaje de JJ Gabriel por el Real Madrid, inminente
articles.standfirst: El club blanco, a punto de oficializar la llegada de la perla inglesa
articles.summary: El club blanco, a punto de oficializar la llegada de la perla inglesa
articles.body: El Real Madrid está a punto de cerrar una operación que ha movilizado a todas las secretarías técnicas de los grandes clubes de Europa. La llegada al club blanco del talento inglés JJ Gabriel, de sólo 16 años, es ya tan sólo una cuestión de tiempo. El Madrid se ha adelantado al resto de grandes trasatlánticos continentales, como PSG, Bayern, City, Chelsea o Barcelona, que se han acercado al entorno del atacante después de que éste decidiera salir del Manchester United. La salida de Gabriel del club de Old Trafford puso en alerta a varios grandes de Europa, cautivados por el talento de un jugador que viene de superar todos los registros de precocidad en el fútbol inglés. Su turbulenta salida del United, y el consiguiente revuelo en relación con el entorno del jugador, no han mermado el interés del Madrid, desde el principio muy bien posicionado para hacerse finalmente con un jugador de incuestionable talento, internacional en todas las categorías de formación de Inglaterra y autor de un hat-trick en su estreno en la Youth League, esta misma temporada. JJ cumplió 16 años el pasado 6 de octubre, una edad clave para desbloquear el complejo proceso de salida del United, club al que llegó en 2022 tras pasar por las canteras de Chelsea, Arsenal y West Ham. Con apenas 11 años, era ya un fenómeno viral por su calidad con el balón en los pies (capaz de dar miles de toques sin dejar caer el balón siendo apenas un crío), y su progresión en Mánchester ha estado a la altura de las expectativas. Debutó con el Sub-18 del United en 2025, con 14 años, con un doblete al Leeds siendo el jugador más joven en vestir esa camiseta en la historia del club. La campaña siguiente anotó 26 goles en 29 partidos y fue elegido mejor futbolista Sub-18 de la Premier League. Ya en este 2026, su estreno en la Youth League lo saldó con un hat-trick ante el Sabah. Rubén Amorim llegó a subirlo a entrenar con el primer equipo y Michael Carrick le dio sus primeros minutos en un amistoso de pretemporada, ante el Atlético de Madrid en Estocolmo. Su falta de continuidad en el primer equipo ha sido el principal argumento empleado por su padre, Joe O'Cearuill, para justificar la salida del chico. O'Cearuill fue futbolista profesional, aunque defensa, no atacante como su hijo, y se ha convertido en el gran arquitecto de la carrera de JJ Gabriel. Desde su cambio de nombre por uno más 'comercial' a la firma de un contrato de patrocinio con Nike, con apenas 14 años, considerado incluso más lucrativo que el que la multinacional estadounidense firmó en su día con el adolescente Neymar. Además de su padre, en la carrera de JJ Gabriel ha sido determinante la figura del agente Ali Barat, fundador de la agencia Epic Sports y bien conocido en el Bernabéu tras el traspaso de Denzel Dumfries al club blanco el pasado verano. Con el horizonte de su 16 cumpleaños ya muy cerca, JJ Gabriel solicitó formalmente su salida del United el pasado mes de septiembre. En las últimas semanas, se está entrenando junto a un preparador personal en España, a la espera de que se cierre un traspaso al Madrid que está ya sólo a falta de firma y comunicado oficial. El United percibirá una cantidad mínima en concepto de derechos de formación (se habla de unas 300.000 libras), pero en Old Trafford se tiran de los pelos por la pérdida de un jugador al que muchos auguran un valor potencial por encima de los 100 millones de euros. De momento, su futuro es el Castilla, pero siempre bajo la supervisión de Mourinho y su staff. La idea es que se transición al primer equipo sea menos turbulenta que la que propició su salida de los 'red devils'.

articles.title: Bordalás: “Está muy difícil el pase pero lo vamos a intentar”
articles.summary: El técnico del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa tras la derrota frente al Brighton y señaló que, pese a que el equipo ha mejorado respecto a las últimas semanas, el pase está “muy difícil”.
articles.body: El técnico del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa tras la derrota frente al Brighton y señaló que, pese a que el equipo ha mejorado respecto a las últimas semanas, el pase está “muy difícil”. Valoración: “No estamos contentos, el equipo ha hecho un gran primer tiempo, ha estado vivo. Ellos han tenido más frescura, hemos pagado el esfuerzo que llevamos haciendo desde el principio, jugadores que iban justos y ese gol nos ha hecho mucho daño. Nos enfrentábamos a un gran equipo, sabíamos que iba a ser difícil, sabemos que está difícil pasar a la siguiente ronda, quedan tres partidos y todavía no está todo hecho”. Equipo reconocible: “Estoy contento en parte, no del todo porque no hemos ganado y, sobre todo, porque hemos vuelto a encajar. Tenemos que corregir ese aspecto, solo hemos sido capaces de dos porterías a cero. El resto, los partidos de Conference y la previa, hemos encajado. Así es muy difícil, no siempre vas a hacer goles. Tenemos que mejorar ese aspecto. Ha sido un error muy grave que estábamos avisando y nos ha costado la derrota”. Físicamente: “Vamos a intentar recuperar a los chicos, hemos acusado en el tramo final, a partir del 70, iban muy justos de fuerza. Es normal porque algunos llegaron a última hora, no han hecho pretemporada. Y esta plantilla no es la del rival, que tiene 47 jugadores en plantilla. Nosotros ahí estamos con 12-13... Aparte de ser el tercero en Premier, es un equipo con un valor de mercado de 700 millones”. Posibilidades: “Sí, las hay, sabemos que está muy difícil, pero cuando llegue el momento. Tenemos un partido muy difícil contra el Villarreal, tremendamente complicado. Cuando llegue el próximo partido en Conference tenemos que darlo todo, a ver si podemos tener suerte y pasar a la siguiente”. Aprovechar las bandas: “Eso nos gustaría, pero no tenemos ningún extremo. Hoy en día es fundamental. Somos el único equipo de Primera, Segunda, 1ª RFEF, 2ª RFEF, 3ª RFEF que no tiene bandas. Hacemos lo que podemos”. Boselli: “Muy bien, ha hecho otro grandísimo partido, ha estado súper atento. Así que hay que vivir los partidos. Estoy muy contento, le felicito pese a la derrota. Ha hecho nuevamente un gran partido, hay que vivir los partidos con esa atención e intensidad. Ojalá siga en esa línea y nos siga ayudando al equipo”.

articles.title: Brilliant Baur, Deadly Duran and Outstanding Osmand
articles.summary: A well earned win under the Paradise lights as Celtic overcome adversity to deservedly beat Besiktas…Celtic finally got off the mark in their Europa League c...
articles.body:
A well earned win under the Paradise lights as Celtic overcome adversity to deservedly beat Besiktas…

Celtic finally got off the mark in their Europa League campaign by defeating Turkish high-flyers Besiktas 3-2 in an entertaining match under at Paradise.

Martin O'Neill surprised a few folk by naming James Forrest in a three man attack alongside Kasper Hogh and Sebastian Tounekti, as well as handing Jordan Lotomba a rare start at right back at the expense of Colby Donovan, and it seemed to most that he'd given up all hope of advancing on the European stage.

To be fair to the players they stuck to the task and showed some grit and determination, something they've been lacking in a while, but it looked like the same old story when the Turkish side opened the scoring from the penalty rebound ten minutes into the second period after Lotomba mistimed a challenge just inside the box.

Sam Johnstone saved Olaitan's effort but the Besiktas front man tucked home the rebound to silence the home crowd, and suddenly we all feared the worst.

But credit to the Celtic players who reacted positively after going a goal behind, as they frantically went in search of an equaliser which duly arrived courtesy of substitute Callum Osmand who scored with his first touch just 43 seconds after being brought on to give the Bhoys a well deserved equaliser, and now it was well and truly game on.

The introduction of Osmand and Camilo Duran rejuvenated the hoops in an attacking sense, and it was the Colombian who fired Celtic in front with just twelve minutes remaining with a unlikely victory now looking like a realistic prospect.

It's never plain sailing with Celtic though, and the Turkish side equalised on the 85th minute thanks to a superb outside of the box effort from Kokcu, and Celtic Park was silenced once again, apart from the visiting supporters who celebrated wildly. Celtic soon burst that Turkish delight turning it into despair.

The atmosphere changed once again just two minutes later when that man Duran struck from close range with what proved to be the winner, and sent the Celtic support home with a much needed smile on their faces.

There's still much needed work to be done if we want to advance from the group stage, but this was a win of vital importance, and one that will give us some much needed confidence after some woeful performances of late.

How good was Mika Baur? Outstanding and a worthy choice as Man of the Match.

articles.title: Mike Elko pushes back on idea Texas A&M has nothing to play for
articles.summary: The Texas A&M Aggies opened the season at No. 8 in the AP poll and reached November at 4-4, with a 1-4 record in the SEC. Head coach Mike Elko sat down at Ru...
articles.body:
The Texas A&M Aggies opened the season at No. 8 in the AP poll and reached November at 4-4, with a 1-4 record in the SEC. Head coach Mike Elko sat down at Rudy's Country Store and BBQ in College Station for Wednesday night's Aggie Football Hour and took on the idea that a season like that has run out of reasons to care.

"I told the guys, 'Listen, we had high expectations for where this thing could go, and obviously we haven't met those, but there's still a massive difference between 4-8 and 8-4.' So when you say there's nothing to play for, in my opinion, there's a lot to play for. There's a lot to play for every single week in terms of continuing to invest in what we started this journey to be about," Elko said, according to On3's Carter Karels.

A year ago, the same program went 11-2 and reached the College Football Playoff. The last time Texas A&M finished 4-8 was 2008, in Mike Sherman's first season, so the low end of Elko's range would be a result no Aggies team has produced in 18 years.

What does Texas A&M still have to play for?

The first College Football Playoff rankings, released on Tuesday, split the Aggies' season cleanly in two. All four losses came against teams in the top 25: the No. 5 Alabama Crimson Tide, No. 6 Kentucky Wildcats, No. 14 LSU Tigers and No. 18 Missouri Tigers. None of the four teams they beat is ranked.

Three of the four games left are against teams in that same group. The Aggies visit the No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks on Saturday, host the No. 13 Tennessee Volunteers on Nov. 14, travel to the Oklahoma Sooners on Nov. 21 and finish against the No. 7 Texas Longhorns at Kyle Field on Nov. 27.

Elko's 8-4 would take a win in all of those games, three of them over the kind of opponent Texas A&M has not beaten this year. If the pattern from the first eight games simply holds, the Aggies would beat Oklahoma, lose the other three and finish 5-7. That makes one upset the difference between staying home in December and playing in a bowl, which is a more concrete answer to the "nothing to play for" crowd than any record Elko named.

Can the Aggies pull off the upset they need?

Texas A&M led 20-17 going into the fourth quarter in Tuscaloosa on Oct. 24, then gained 15 yards over its final three possessions, all three-and-outs, in a 31-20 loss. Marcel Reed threw two interceptions that day, and Elko considered a change at quarterback before sticking with him. "I still believe he's our best option," Elko said.

Elko has been making some form of this case since the 27-6 loss at Missouri on Oct. 10, when the offense failed to score a touchdown. "We're in a really bad spot right now, but we'll work our way out of it," Elko said that night.

The Aggies have since beaten The Citadel, lost to Alabama and used an open week to work through their problems. Two wins would make them bowl eligible, and the first chance comes at 3 p.m. ET on Saturday on ESPN at Williams-Brice Stadium.

articles.title: Girls state soccer: Blake outlasts Mahtomedi to reach state final
articles.summary: After more than 70 minutes, Blake got the go-ahead goal Thursday to secure a 1-0 win over Mahtomedi in their state Class 2A semifinal at U.S. Bank Stadium. S...
articles.body:
After more than 70 minutes, Blake got the go-ahead goal Thursday to secure a 1-0 win over Mahtomedi in their state Class 2A semifinal at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Sophomore midfielder Lauren Breyer's perfectly placed ball off an assist from Ellen Rippe found the corner of the goal to send the top-seeded Bears (18-2-0) into Saturday's championship game against No. 2 seed Holy Angels (18-1-1).

"We knew we needed to score in the second half. After Rippe found me the ball, I just knew I had to place it," Breyer said.

Goalie Reese Aafedt fought off multiple Zephyrs attacks at the net throughout each half.

"Reese and coach Emma Gumlia have been working for the last two years on high balls, under the crossbar, and Mahtomedi had a free kick," Bears coach Jocelyn Keller said. "Reese was prepared and (she) made a save on a dime, and it kept us in the game."

"We had a half dozen really good opportunities, and it was a really nice way to finish the way we did with less than 10 minutes left," Blake head coach Jocelyn Keller said, "Definitely a team win."

Last year, the Bears fell to Mahtomedi 1-0. This year, it was their chance to flip the script.

"We were under a lot of pressure against a really skilled team. We just had to get to a different level today, and it didn't happen," Zephyrs head coach David Wald said.

The Bears are hoping to carry one thing over to their championship match at 12:30 p.m. Saturday at U.S. Bank Stadium.

"Continuing to support each other and being positive on the field," Breyer said. "During the second half, we were really supporting each other, and I feel like we saw that energy boost."

articles.title: LSU QB Sam Leavitt reveals what he hears from fans before Alabama game
articles.summary: LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt has been in Baton Rouge for less than a year, after arriving from the Arizona State Sun Devils in the offseason, and Louis...
articles.body:
LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt has been in Baton Rouge for less than a year, after arriving from the Arizona State Sun Devils in the offseason, and Louisiana has already made sure he knows what Saturday means.

Speaking to reporters at LSU's player availability on Tuesday, he described how the message finds him on ordinary errands before the Alabama Crimson Tide come to Tiger Stadium.

"It's going to be the biggest game of the year. I hear all the time if I'm going to the store to grab something, getting food or whatever, they're saying, 'Hey, go beat Bama.' So, you know, obviously it means a lot, and for me to be in this position, being a little kid, looking back, and if someone told me 'Bama was playing LSU on Saturday, I was going to be watching that game. So, being from the West Coast and fantasizing about watching a game down here, now being a part of it, it's a surreal and special experience," Leavitt said.

Leavitt grew up in West Linn, Oregon, where he was 14 when LSU beat Alabama 46-41 in 2019. The people stopping him at the store have a more recent game in mind. Alabama has won three straight in the series since LSU's 32-31 overtime win in Baton Rouge in 2022, including a 42-13 win at Tiger Stadium in 2024 and a 20-9 win in Tuscaloosa last November. Saturday is also Lane Kiffin's first shot at the Crimson Tide as LSU's head coach.

Why does Sam Leavitt's 'biggest game' claim hold up for LSU?

The selection committee put LSU at No. 14 in Tuesday's first College Football Playoff rankings, two spots outside the top 12. The next three weeks bring No. 5 Alabama, the No. 7 Texas Longhorns and a trip to the No. 13 Tennessee Volunteers, which means a loss on Saturday would send a three-loss team into the Texas game. Every quarterback calls the next opponent the biggest of the year at some point, and Leavitt's version comes with a schedule that backs him.

Leavitt was less interested in the committee's number when asked about it. "I really don't care. At the end of the day, we've got to go win games. We could be 1 or 50, and if we go win or lose the next five or four, that ranking doesn't even apply," Leavitt said , according to Tiger Rag's Glenn Guilbeau.

LSU sits nine spots behind Alabama in those rankings and was still a six-point favorite at BetMGM on Monday. The Tigers have the No. 6 offense in the country at 510 yards per game, and they scored 31 and 38 in their last two games, wins over the Mississippi State Bulldogs and Auburn Tigers.

"I think it's going to be the best defense we played. There's not really many holes, and their DC does a great job. They play really hard. They go after the ball, so it's going to be a very emotional and a high-stakes game. And I'm really excited to go play against them," Leavitt said .

Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, the first daytime meeting between the teams in Tiger Stadium since LSU's 24-21 win in 2010.

articles.title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti Reacts to 1st CFP Rankings, Calls Out SEC Bias over Big Ten
articles.summary: Indiana might be the only Big Ten team without reason to complain about the initial College Football Playoff rankings, but head coach Curt Cignetti still wasn't happy with the overall picture.
articles.body:
Indiana might be the only Big Ten team without reason to complain about the initial College Football Playoff rankings, but head coach Curt Cignetti still wasn't happy with the overall picture.

"Come on," he said while laughing during his Wednesday radio show after he was asked for his thoughts on the rankings (h/t David Ubben of The Athletic).

"These people, and there's a whole bunch of them, they march out of the tent and they're given instructions on what to say and they follow the company line," he said in an apparent reference to the love the SEC received in the rankings and the conference's coverage. "And I don't need to go any further."

Indiana checked in at No. 4 in the first rankings despite having zero wins against any other teams in the Top 25. It lost to Ohio State in its only matchup against a team that is currently ranked, but the Buckeyes are eight spots lower at No. 12 despite the head-to-head result.

Ohio State has a second loss, which came in the nonconference portion of its schedule by a single point against Texas while the Hoosiers played North Texas, Howard and Western Kentucky before Big Ten play.

Still, Indiana has played a number of teams above .500, as Cignetti pointed out:

He also criticized the coverage the SEC received and said on his radio show, "SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum. And that's why you see all these SEC teams up there and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high."

Cignetti's comments come after the SEC received a number of favorable rankings.

UCLA, which is undefeated, is No. 8 and behind one-loss Georgia, two-loss Alabama, one-loss Kentucky and two-loss Texas. What's more, two-loss Ole Miss is also ahead of one-loss Notre Dame and two-loss Ohio State.

In all, the SEC has 10 teams compared to the Big Ten's six in the Top 25. The Big Ten may also have some trouble getting a high number of teams in the field, as three of those six teams are ranked 19th and below.

It is rather jarring considering the Big Ten's overall dominance in the modern-era of college football with NIL and the transfer portal. Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana have won the last three national championships, while the conference as a whole has been much better than the SEC in the actual CFP games:

Ultimately, the Hoosiers and perhaps the Bruins, Buckeyes and other Big Ten teams will have a chance to play things out on the field if they take care of their own games in November.

But Cignetti is frustrated with the initial rankings.

articles.title: Notre Dame vs. Miami: One fatal flaw could decide everything
articles.summary: Notre Dame desperately needs a win against Miami, and they could have one key edge.
articles.body:
It's safe to say the College Football Playoff selection committee isn't thrilled with what Notre Dame has done this season.

They knocked the Irish down to No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP poll, this week. That sent a strong message that Notre Dame still has to earn their full trust.

The perfect opportunity comes as the Week 10 college football games kick off. The Fighting Irish will host No. 1 ranked Miami in a clash of the titans under the lights.

Not having Malachi Toney on the field is already one major edge in Notre Dame's favor. The star Miami wideout is dealing with a new ankle injury that will sideline him. Not that it's stopping the Irish from preparing for him anyway.

But there's one other major flaw in this matchup the Golden Domers can exploit.

The biggest flaw one team can exploit is Miami's vulnerability in pass coverage, which Notre Dame can attack with quarterback CJ Carr and its receiving corps.

For all the Hurricanes do well, defending the pass isn't one of them. They rank just 121st among 138 FBS teams by allowing 252 yards in the air per game.

Miami allowed 341 air yards and earned a rock-bottom 30.1 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, their lowest mark in 12 years, after a narrow win at North Carolina.

While the Canes boast one of the nation's best run-stops, opposing teams have pivoted heavily to short, quick perimeter passes to neutralize their front seven. Miami has also struggled finishing tackles, missing more than a dozen against UNC.

Notre Dame has been efficient putting the ball in the air this season. It has just one interception, covers more than 8 yards per pass, and hits 67 percent of its passes.

The Irish passing offense should attack with:

Quick passes: Use slants, crossing routes and short outs to get receivers into space.

Tempo: Prevent Miami from comfortably substituting and disguising coverages.

Yards after catch: Make Miami's defensive backs tackle in space rather than simply defend the initial throw.

Carr has struggled with deep-ball accuracy recently, completing just 4 of 24 passes traveling at least 15 air yards over his last two games.

Notre Dame will need to emphasize rhythm throws and easy completions rather than relying on low-percentage deep shots.

The key matchup: Can Miami's secondary hold up against Notre Dame's short and intermediate passing game?

If it can't, Notre Dame will have to sustain long drives and keep Miami's explosive offense off the field.

articles.title: BYU HC Kalani Sitake gets honest about himself ahead of Utah game
articles.summary: BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake joined The Triple Option this week, the college football show hosted by Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II and Rob Stone, ahead...
articles.body:
BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake joined The Triple Option this week, the college football show hosted by Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II and Rob Stone, ahead of Saturday's trip to the No. 3 Utah Utes. He brought a 7-1 record and a No. 9 spot in the first College Football Playoff rankings with him, and he still used the appearance to grade himself.

"I need to do a better job as a head coach to make sure that we play at our best. We're 7-1 right now, and I have not done a good enough job where I feel like we've played consistently at our best. And so that's my focus for this team. I think we can do that. I know we've had some injuries that may play into it a little bit, but the standard's the same. And I think the young guys got to grow up. We have to trust more people. We have to trust each other. Be assignment sound at 1/11. Everyone does their part, and then the good things can happen from that. So I'm going to go back to the basics, the fundamentals, the simple things that can get us there because that's what we can control, and that's what I can control as a head coach," Sitake said.

Sitake has been delivering versions of that message since the final seconds of a 27-20 win over the Arizona State Sun Devils on Oct. 31. "I'd like to just get in a position where we don't have to worry about the clock and worry about stuff like that. That's my job. I've got to get these guys ready to roll and get them playing at a higher level," Sitake said after the game, according to KSL's Jaxon Wynder.

What has Kalani Sitake seen from BYU that a 7-1 record hides?

BYU led Arizona State 17-3 at halftime with six sacks against Jake Fette, a backup quarterback making his first career start. The Cougars did not sack him again, and the Sun Devils tied the game at 17 in the third quarter. BYU finished with 47 rushing yards, its lowest total of the season, and converted 3 of 13 third downs. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier carried it 16 times for 15 yards, twice as many attempts as running back Sione Moa.

The week before, the Cougars were No. 2 in the AP poll when they lost 39-31 in double overtime to the UCF Knights. Six days later, UCF lost 41-9 at home to the Baylor Bears. Five of BYU's seven wins have come by 14 points or fewer, including a 28-24 win over the Notre Dame Fighting Irish, so a coach who says his team has not played consistently well has plenty of game film on his side.

"After watching the film, there were quite a bit of missed assignments, guys not doing their part. The running game can't just be all on the running back or even the O line. It takes all 11 guys on the field doing their part. … My job as head coach is to make sure that we're consistently at our best, and I haven't done a good enough job at that, but we'll get there. It's taken longer than I expected. Sometimes you're dealing with different players in there and different injuries and things like that," Sitake said Monday.

Can BYU get back to basics in time for Utah?

Star running back LJ Martin has missed four straight games with an ankle injury and is questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Evan Johnson sprained his left ankle against UCF, missed the Arizona State game and is off this week's depth chart. True freshman Journee Tonga is listed third at running back after gaining 2 yards on two carries against the Sun Devils, which leaves a first-year back close to a bigger role in the week Sitake says the young guys have to grow up.

Kickoff is noon ET on Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium, in the first top-10 matchup in the history of the rivalry. Utah is 8-0, and Sitake described what his team is walking into at the same Monday briefing. "We are going into a tough environment (against) a tough team, and facing a dynamic defense that does a lot of great things. They cause havoc, and they are really sound," Sitake said .
